items.title: OpenAI says its AI went rogue and launched 'unprecedented' cyber-attack - BBC
items.summary: # OpenAI says its AI went rogue and launched 'unprecedented' cyber-attack. OpenAI has revealed some of its most advanced AI models went rogue and hacked a start-up after it lost control of them during a security test. The ChatGPT-maker said its agents - AI bots which can operate alone after some human instruction – were being tested in a controlled environment, but found vulnerabilities and managed to escape. OpenAI said the incident was "unprecedented", and it was working with Hugging Face to investigate what happened and strengthen safeguards. Gina Neff, head of the Minderoo Centre for Technology and Democracy at the University of Cambridge, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that the security tests - called sandboxes - are "supposed to be secure environments where you can see what the models are capable of". Once outside, the AI identified Hugging Face as a likely source of the answers they were seeking in the test, and tried to gain access.

items.title: OpenAI launches its new family of models with GPT-5.6 - TechCrunch
items.summary: # OpenAI launches its new family of models with GPT-5.6. OpenAI unveiled its newest family of models on Thursday, introducing a new set of heavyweight programs into an increasingly crowded field of AI offerings. CEO Sam Altman has promised that his company’s newest models are orders of magnitude more efficient and cost-effective than previous versions, recently telling CNBC that Sol is 54% more token efficient when it comes to AI coding tasks. However, GPT-5.6 and its attendant marketing seems most designed to take aim at OpenAI’s primary opponent, Anthropic. Anthropic has managed to make itself the likable underdog of the AI race, focusing fixedly on enterprise customers and winning a growing share of support as a result. Not to be outdone, OpenAI cites the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, a notable benchmarking metric, to claim that its latest family of models outshines Anthropic’s models at every turn. OpenAI calls Sol its “best coding model yet,” and has explicitly compared it to Anthropic’s recently released (and much hyped) Fable.

items.title: Apple sues OpenAI, alleging trade secrets theft from former employees - San Francisco Chronicle
items.summary: # Apple sues OpenAI, alleging trade secrets theft from former employees. Apple sued OpenAI on Friday, alleging former Apple employees stole trade secrets after joining the artificial intelligence startup. The suit filed in Northern California federal court alleged OpenAI executive Tang Tan “directed job candidates still working for Apple to bring ‘actual parts’ from Apple to their interviews for ‘show and tell’ sessions in which he and his team at OpenAI can elicit still more Apple confidential information.” Apple also alleged OpenAI worker Chang Liu stole an Apple laptop and other hardware. The iPhone maker alleged that “at every level, from members of its Technical Staff to its Chief Hardware Officer, and in coordination with business partners, OpenAI has been stealing Apple’s trade secrets and confidential information.”. Apple and OpenAI previously partnered in 2024 to bring the ChatGPT chatbot into iPhones, but the Cupertino company is now working with OpenAI archrival Google and its Gemini AI model.

items.title: OpenAI appoints two new members to board of directors - CNBC
items.summary: * OpenAI said it's appointed longtime financial executives David Vélez and Robin Vince to its nonprofit and for-profit boards. * OpenAI carried out a recapitalization in October that solidified its structure as a nonprofit, called the OpenAI Foundation, with a controlling stake in its for-profit business. OpenAI said it appointed longtime financial executives David Vélez and Robin Vince to its nonprofit and for-profit boards of directors, as the company marches closer to a prospective IPO. Vélez is the CEO of Nubank, the largest digital bank in Latin America, and Vince is the CEO of the financial services company BNY. OpenAI carried out a recapitalization in October that solidified its structure as a nonprofit, called the OpenAI Foundation, with a controlling stake in its for-profit business, the OpenAI Group PBC. "David and Robin are exceptional leaders who have used technology to reshape financial services and expand opportunity at global scale," Bret Taylor, chair of the OpenAI Foundation and OpenAI Group PBC Boards, said in a statement.

items.title: Apple files lawsuit accusing ChatGPT maker OpenAI of stealing trade secrets - Greenwich Time
items.summary: # Apple files lawsuit accusing ChatGPT maker OpenAI of stealing trade secrets. Apple on Friday accused OpenAI of stealing trade secrets as it seeks to build its own hardware for ChatGPT, a major rupture in a partnership between the iPhone maker and the artificial intelligence company. Apple said in the lawsuit filed in a California federal court that the theft of its trade secrets was part of a “coordinated pattern of misconduct at an institutional level” by OpenAI. “This case is about Apple’s former employees stealing Apple’s trade secrets for the benefit of OpenAI,” the filing says. Apple said it began investigating whether some of its confidential information was compromised and “uncovered a pattern of theft” of Apple’s trade secrets by former employees who moved on to positions at OpenAI. Apple said in the lawsuit that it reached out to OpenAI in February to raise its concerns early in its investigation, but said that OpenAI did not respond.

items.title: A three-hour video about medieval history became part of a $100,000/month sleep-content machine.
items.summary:
A three-hour video about medieval history became part of a $100,000/month sleep-content machine.

The person behind it is Leo.

He runs Sleepless Historian, a YouTube channel with 887,000 subscribers built for viewers who want to fall asleep, not stay engaged with every second.

That changes the usual content equation.

A normal creator cuts anything that feels too slow. Leo needs the video to remain slow, calm and predictable because the viewer is using it as part of a nightly routine. The narration can continue for hours while medieval scenes loop quietly underneath it.

AI makes that length economical.

ChatGPT and Subscribr produce scripts long enough for 60-minute narrations. ElevenLabs creates the British voiceover. Leonardo AI handles the medieval imagery. CapCut and Artlist turn the pieces into a finished upload.

The result reportedly brings in around $100,000 a month from YouTube ads.

Most creators think long watch time comes from making people unable to look away.

Leo found a format where viewers can close their eyes and leave the video running.

items.title: 22 yaşındaki bir İspanyol kızı, ChatGPT'ye 12 dolarlık bir domain buldurdu. 17 gün sonra, Silikon Vadisi'nden bir girişi
items.summary:
22 yaşındaki bir İspanyol kızı, ChatGPT'ye 12 dolarlık bir domain buldurdu. 17 gün sonra, Silikon Vadisi'nden bir girişimci ondan 13.000 dolara satın aldı.

İstek basitti:

"Bana henüz kimsenin bilmediği, ama 30 gün içinde patlayacak bir teknoloji terimi bul. (…) .com'un müsait olup olmadığını kontrol et. Basit tut."

ChatGPT, ona 9 dakikada küçük bir scraper yazdı. Kız, botu telefonundan çalıştırdı. Ve hepsi bu kadar.

1.Gün Bot bir terim yakaladı: "synthetic memory". Uzman bir podcast'te 23 kez bahsedilmiş. Twitter'da sıfır. Kız, öğle yemeği aralığında 14 dolara (…).com'u satın aldı.

2.Gün Terim, Hacker News ana sayfasında göründü. Telefonu direkt mesajlarla dolup taştı.

3.Gün Menlo Park'ten bir girişimci masaya 13.000 dolar koydu. Kız pazarlığı bitirmedi. 13.000 dolar + 80 bin takipçisi olan adamın hesabından bir teşekkür tweet'i de istedi ve aldı.

Aynı gün, 10 saniyelik kısa bir video çekti. Sadece gülümsüyor. Elinde telefon, ekranda satış onayı. Üstünde tek bir yazı:

14 dolar → 13.000 dolar. 16. gün ChatGPT'ye sadece bir soru sordu.

Video 4,9 milyon izlenme aldı. Binlerce kişi yorumlara tek bir kelime yazdı: SIGNAL.

Kızın tek cümlesi şu:

"Hızlı olmak, zengin olmaktan iyidir. Bunu kanıtlamak istedim."
